items.title: Explained: 13 reasons why the Nifty could not deliver more in last 5 years
items.description: Over a five-year period, thirteen stocks within the Nifty index adversely affected its overall performance, resulting in negative returns for these specific laggards. Conversely, the Nifty 50 index itself witnessed gains. Had these underperforming stocks been excluded, the index's returns would have been significantly enhanced. Active mutual funds, benefiting from reduced exposure to these stocks, ultimately outperformed the Nifty 50, highlighting the advantage for actively managed funds during this timeframe.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: On Monday, Indian equity markets experienced a positive turn, with the Nifty 50 index rising due to a dip in crude oil prices and widespread purchasing among investors. While foreign portfolio investors sold off shares, domestic institutional players significantly increased their stakes. The Indian Rupee showed strength, aided by the lower crude oil rates.

items.title: Stocks in news: ONGC, Lloyds Metals, Canara Bank, Rays of Belief and GRSE
items.description: Indian stock markets closed higher on Monday, with the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex gaining points. Several companies, including ONGC and Canara Bank, are expected to be active on Tuesday. ONGC announced a gas discovery in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin, while Canara Bank received a rating from Moody’s. Lloyds Metals and Energy approved capacity expansion, and Suryoday Small Finance Bank plans to raise funds.

items.title: Bandhan Bank promoter to gradually reduce stake to meet RBI norms
items.description: Bandhan Financial Services will reduce its stake in Bandhan Bank gradually.  The promoter aims to comply with RBI regulations by 2030.  Recent share sales occurred on the open market, lowering holdings.  A proposed stock split will divide shares to attract retail investors.  Shareholders will review this plan at the upcoming annual general meeting.

items.title: Government may do away with UPI subsidies as MDR revenue kicks in
items.description: Government may end UPI subsidies for small transactions as merchant fees are introduced.  Taxpayer-funded incentives for UPI and RuPay transactions are being phased out.  No new subsidies have been paid for transactions since April 2025.  This shift aims to make the payment ecosystem self-sustaining and reduce taxpayer burden.  Incentive disbursements have significantly decreased in recent fiscal years.

items.title: Motilal Oswal initiates Buy on Solar Industries, sees 24% upside. 4 reasons why
items.description: Motilal Oswal has initiated coverage on Solar Industries with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 23,000, citing strong growth prospects across explosives and defence. The brokerage expects revenue and profit to grow at 43% and 34% CAGR, respectively, through FY30.

items.title: Pace Digitek shares jump 13% after subsidiary bags Rs 488 crore BESS order
items.description: Pace Digitek shares surged over 13% to Rs 175.37 on Tuesday after its material subsidiary, Lineage Power, bagged a Rs 488.46-crore BESS order from NTPC GE Power Services. The project at the Barh Super Thermal Power Project involves BESS containers, maintenance, and extended warranty through December 2026.

items.title: Oracle Financial among 4 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of September 21, four stocks in the NSE F&O segment recorded a rise of more than 8% in futures open interest compared with the previous trading session. A notable increase in futures open interest indicates a substantial rise in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a security. This can reflect market participants initiating new positions or increasing the size of existing positions.

items.title: Sensex rises 110 points, Nifty above 23,450 as oil prices, bond yields cool down. Time for a sectoral pivot?
items.description: Indian equities traded higher as softer crude prices and easing bond yields improved sentiment. Sensex and Nifty extended gains, while broader markets also advanced. Analysts highlighted a possible sectoral shift towards fairly valued largecaps and improving technical momentum.

items.title: This stock just beat AI star HFCL’s 230% rally to top Nifty 500 gainers in 2026. Can outperformance last?
items.description: Welspun Corp has emerged as the top-performing Nifty 500 stock in 2026 after a 236% rally, overtaking AI infrastructure play HFCL. The sharp gains have been driven by strong investor interest in the company’s oil, gas and water transmission business. The key question now is whether the rally can sustain.

items.title: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy shares rally 8% after securing Rs 985 crore domestic and global orders
items.description: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy shares surged nearly 8% on Tuesday to Rs 186.66 after winning domestic and international orders exceeding Rs 985 crore. The orders include a 534.3 MWp solar project in Rajasthan and a 616 MWh energy storage capacity project in South Africa.

items.title: Waaree Energies shares gain 2% after company bags 2 GW solar module order
items.description: Waaree Energies shares rose after securing a 2 GW solar module supply order from a leading domestic solar developer for FY27-FY28. The contract’s value remains undisclosed. Despite the order, the stock has declined recently and trades below seven of eight SMAs. FIIs raised their June-quarter stake, while mutual fund holdings fell.

items.title: Tata Group stocks see sharp swings as boardroom battle intensifies, but analysts say avoid the noise
items.description: Tata Group stocks are undergoing substantial fluctuations amid an unsettling boardroom conflict as Tata Trusts questions the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as Chairman. Market analysts advise investors to hone in on the core fundamentals and disregard the temporary corporate commotion. Companies like Tata Steel and Tata Motors are highlighted as sound investment choices, showing promise for long-term growth and accumulation due to their solid performance.

items.title: Polycab shares slide 17% in 3 months amid Ultravolt shock, but Jefferies sees 33% upside. What’s behind the bullish view?
items.description: Polycab shares have fallen 17% from their June peak after UltraTech entered the wires and cables segment. Jefferies retained its Buy rating and Rs 11,100 target, implying 33% upside, citing strong demand, volume growth and Polycab’s distribution strength.

items.title: Goldman Sachs raises target on a stock that has already surged over 140% this year. Do you own it?
items.description: Sansera Engineering shares rallied after Goldman Sachs raised its target price to Rs 4,990 from Rs 4,500 while retaining its Buy rating. The revised target implies 16.1% upside, with the stock already up over 140% in 2026. Goldman sees investments by Applied Materials and Lam Research in India supporting local supplier ecosystems and R&D, potentially driving longer-term growth for Sansera’s ADS component business.

items.title: Syngene International among 4 stocks that closed crossing above VWAP
items.description: On September 21, the closing prices of four stocks in the Nifty 500 pack were more than 1.5% above their respective VWAPs (Volume Weighted Average Price), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. When the closing price is above the VWAP, it means the stock closed at a price higher than its volume-weighted average traded price during the day. The VWAP gives greater weight to prices at which higher trading volumes occurred.

items.title: Cohance Lifesciences among 5 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On September 21, five stocks in the Nifty500 pack were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. "RSI trending up" means that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, suggesting strengthening momentum in the stock's price. This can indicate potential upward movement and may be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Moneyview pays Rs 160 crore incentive to CEO ahead of IPO; FY26 profit takes 30% hit
items.description: IPO-bound Moneyview paid CEO Puneet Agarwal a one-time Rs 160 crore performance incentive in FY26, reducing reported net profit by about Rs 120 crore after tax. The company said the payment was non-recurring and has no plans for similar incentives. Moneyview’s Rs 1,092-crore IPO opens September 24 at Rs 32-34.

items.title: Engineers India among 4 stocks showing White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On September 21, four Nifty500 stocks appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level towards the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.

items.title: Pine Labs shares rise after Rs 934 crore block deal; Mastercard likely sells stake
items.description: Mastercard Asia Pacific is approximately selling its entire Pine Labs stake.  This block deal involves 49.7 million shares valued up to Rs 892.5 crore.  The transaction floor price is set at Rs 179.50 per share.  Citigroup Global Markets India is managing the placement as the sole agent.  The deal is expected to settle on September 23.

items.title: Stock Radar: Sansera Engineering stock hits fresh record highs in September; time to buy or book profits?
items.description: Sansera Engineering stock has broken out of a recent consolidation range and hit a fresh record high, with bullish momentum supported by moving averages, RSI and MACD. Analysts see further upside towards Rs 5,150, with a closing-basis stop loss at Rs 3,800.
